Question B-007-004-011.

Why the correct answer is right: Multiple paths can arrive at different phases and delays. Besides strength fading, that can distort the phase relationship of the received signal.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Frequency shift": Frequency shift would mean the signal is moved in frequency; multipath fading mainly changes amplitude and phase.
- sourceIndex 2: "Heterodyne squeal": Heterodyne squeal comes from another carrier or oscillator beat, not from ordinary two-path propagation.
- sourceIndex 3: "Higher noise floor": Higher noise floor is a noise condition; multipath can degrade a signal even when the receiver noise has not increased.
